paragraphs: Burford is the world's largest dedicated provider of capital, based on portfolio size, against the underlying value of litigation and legal assets, which we colloquially call legal finance.

We are a global firm that serves the legal industry by providing an array of financial products and services. Our largest business is providing capital to clients engaged in ongoing legal disputes, which they can use both to pay the legal fees and expenses associated with disputes and to monetize the expected future value of disputes. Our focus is on large, complex disputes, not on small-scale litigation typically pursued by consumers or small businesses. We rarely engage in transactions in which we are providing less than $5.0 million in capital, and we frequently provide multiples of that amount up to hundreds of millions of dollars. Since our inception in 2009, we made commitments of more than $12.1 billion into legal finance assets on a group-wide basis.

Our clients include a wide range of the world's largest businesses and law firms. Legal finance allows litigants to hire the firm of their choice without incurring upfront fees and to accelerate a portion of an expected recovery on the business's preferred schedule. Further, legal finance may enable litigants to avoid incurring legal fees as an operating expense, and thus improve net income metrics, as well as boost liquidity by obtaining cash through upfront monetization of legal assets that otherwise would not be reflected in their financial statements. Legal finance allows law firms to obtain cash to operate their businesses and pay the salaries of their lawyers even when they have taken a case on a contingent fee or alternative fee basis. It also allows law firms that prefer to operate on an hourly basis to compete for contingency or alternative fee work. We have received financing inquiries or engaged on potential new business with 95 of the 100 largest US law firms by revenue according to the 2025 rankings by The American Lawyer and 93 of the 100 largest global law firms by revenue according to the 2025 rankings by The American Lawyer as well as large regional firms and litigation boutiques.

We fund our legal finance portfolio primarily from our balance sheet using modest leverage, with the aim of re-investing proceeds to grow and compound returns. Our principal financing activities are supplemented by the use of third-party capital through private funds, from which we earn asset management income.

Today, we manage a group-wide legal finance portfolio of $7.5 billion. Our portfolio is diversified by geography and type of legal claim and is, we believe, the largest of its kind globally. Over the last 16 years, it has grown by a multiple of more than 50x when compared to $130 million raised at our inception.

In an industry that continues to grow and evolve, we believe we enjoy a substantial competitive advantage, given our lifetime track record of generating strong returns, our growing proprietary data set drawn from thousands of cases that guides optimal underwriting decisions, our balance sheet scale, our diversity of funding, our quality of team and our brand recognition.
In addition to legal finance, we see opportunity and potential growth for our company in providing certain additional service offerings within the business of law.

We are composed of our parent company, Burford Capital Limited, and numerous wholly owned subsidiaries in various jurisdictions through which our operations are conducted and our capital is deployed. Burford Capital LLC is a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Burford Capital Limited and our primary operating company in the United States, and Burford Capital (UK) Limited is a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Burford Capital Limited and our primary operating company in the United Kingdom. These two entities provide various corporate and investment advisory services to other group companies. Our parent company, Burford Capital Limited, does not have any operations or employees. See "—Organizational structure" for additional information with respect to our organizational structure.

In 2009, our founders launched Burford with a shared vision of an entity supported by permanent capital that could provide bespoke financing to help businesses and law firms address the significant economic challenges they faced in managing legal costs. At the time, the few capital providers addressing this investment proposition were generally domiciled in the United Kingdom, where prior judicial system reforms had permitted the entry of third-party capital into the delivery of a range of legal services. Thus, despite the investment adviser's team being based in the United States, Burford Capital Limited was incorporated in the Bailiwick of Guernsey ("Guernsey") as a closed-end fund company limited by shares on September 11, 2009 with a view to list the vehicle on the London Stock Exchange through an offering of new shares. Following

Increased demand for our capital proposition soon meant the closed-end fund structure was insufficient to address the market opportunity. In 2012, our shareholders voted in support of a proposal to reconstitute Burford as a unitary, specialty finance operating company. The reconstitution permitted more debt capital to be raised to fund growth than was possible under the closed-end fund vehicle. Between 2014 and 2018, we raised $693.0 million through the sale of bonds listed on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange, and the fair value of our capital provision assets grew by more than 6x. Outgrowing the UK bond market's capacity to provide the US dollar funding needed to match the principal currency denomination of our legal finance assets, we sought credit ratings to facilitate access to the US private debt market and we duly obtained a maiden corporate family rating from Moody's in October 2019 and a long-term debt rating from Standard & Poor's in November 2019.

We have also made strategic acquisitions to support inorganic growth. Our acquisition in 2011 of Firstassist Legal Expenses Insurance, a leading provider of litigation expenses insurance in the United Kingdom, provided footprint in London and was the basis of our legacy adverse cost insurance business. Our acquisition in 2015 of a business intelligence firm Focus Intelligence Ltd enabled us to provide clients judgment enforcement services for their funded disputes. Our acquisition in 2016 of GKC Holdings, LLC, a law-focused asset manager registered as an investment adviser with the SEC, formed the initial core of our asset management business as well as expanded our US footprint and our ability to finance patent disputes.

To support further development of our standing in US capital markets, in 2020, Burford Capital Limited registered with the SEC as a "foreign private issuer", which, among other things, allowed us to issue annual consolidated financial statements on Form 20-F and interim condensed consolidated financial statements on Form 6-K and exempted us from certain provisions applicable to US domestic public companies. We secured the admission of our ordinary shares on the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE") on October 19, 2020, also under the symbol "BUR". Subsequently, our subsidiaries issued $1.4 billion of debt securities through private placement transactions under Rule 144A and Regulation S under the Securities Act. See note 12 (Debt) to our consolidated financial statements contained in this 2025 Form 10-K for additional information with respect to our debt securities.

Upon determining that the majority of our ordinary shares were held in the United States as of June 30, 2024, we no longer qualified as a "foreign private issuer" effective as of January 1, 2025. We are now subject to the same disclosure and financial reporting requirements as most US domestic public companies listed on the NYSE.
We maintain our registered address at Oak House, Hirzel Street, St. Peter Port, Guernsey GY1 2NP. Our telephone number at our registered address is +44 1481 723 450.

paragraphs: Investing in our securities involves risk. Persons investing in our securities should carefully consider the risks set forth below and the other information contained in this 2025 Form 10-K and our other reports that we file with, or furnish to, the SEC from time to time, including our consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Any of the following risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or liquidity. Our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or liquidity could also be materially and adversely affected by additional factors that apply to all companies generally as well as other risks that are not currently known to us or that we currently view to be immaterial. In any such case, the trading price of our securities could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment in our securities. While we may attempt to mitigate known risks to the extent we believe to be practicable and reasonable, we can provide no assurance, and we make no representation, that our mitigation efforts, if any, will be successful. See "Forward-looking statements", "Business" and "Management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations" for additional information with respect to certain business, competitive, regulatory, market, economic and other conditions that may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or liquidity.

▪Our success depends on our ability to identify and select suitable legal finance assets to finance, and our failure to do so could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or liquidity.

▪Our business and operations could suffer if we are not able to prevent improper use or disclosure of, or access to, privileged information, intellectual property or litigation or business strategy due to cybersecurity breaches, unauthorized use or theft.

▪The inaccuracy or failure of the probabilistic model and decision science tools, including AI technologies, we use to predict the returns on our legal finance assets and in our operations could have a material adverse effect on our business.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations is for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. This discussion should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes thereto contained elsewhere in this 2025 Form 10-K.

The following discussion and analysis also contain a discussion of certain unaudited KPIs (as defined below) and non-GAAP financial measures that are used by management to monitor our financial condition and results of operations. These KPIs and non-GAAP financial measures are supplemental and should not be considered in isolation from, as substitutes for, or superior to, our consolidated financial condition or results of operations as reported under US GAAP. See "—Basis of presentation of financial information" and "—Reconciliations" for additional information with respect to KPIs and non-GAAP financial measures and the applicable reconciliations.

The discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2024, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, can be found in the "Management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations" section of our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, which was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 3, 2025.

Our portfolio returns are driven by judicial activity, and we believe these returns are generally uncorrelated to market conditions or the performance of the overall economy. The most direct impact of economic and market conditions on our business relates to our cost of debt and ease of access to corporate debt capital markets, as well as movements in market rates that cause adjustments to the discount rates applied in the fair value of our assets and that impact our quarterly revenue recognition in accordance with US GAAP. We believe that we maintain access to corporate debt capital markets, supported by credit rating upgrades from Moody's in the second quarter of 2025 and from S&P in the third quarter of 2025 and as demonstrated by successful debt offerings in July 2025 and January 2026. Overall, we believe our business model is
particularly resilient to economic and market cycles due to the nature of the assets that drive our revenues and cash flow.

More broadly, economic conditions can have an impact on the volume and type of litigation that we may consider financing. For example, increased rates of corporate insolvencies can lead to opportunities to finance litigation relating to or arising out of insolvencies and bankruptcies; higher interest rates or other forms of economic stress can cause businesses to act illegally (such as to conspire to fix prices) leading to financeable claims; and pressure from shareholders and markets can lead to the commission of securities fraud and other similar acts, again resulting in financeable claims.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, the rising potential for global trade disruption through the implementation of tariffs drove significant volatility in global financial markets. We do not believe that a broad elevation in global tariff rates would have a significant impact on the performance of our legal finance portfolio or our financial results. While the economic impact of trade tariffs is uncertain at this point, tighter financial conditions and a weakening of gross domestic product would typically cause the incidence of corporate disputes and associated litigation to increase, although it is usual for this to occur with a lag.

See "Risk factors—Risks relating to our business and industry—We are subject to credit risk relating to our various legal finance assets that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or liquidity" and "Risk factors—Risks relating to our business and industry—Legal, political and economic uncertainty surrounding the effects, severity and duration of public health threats could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or liquidity".

Court systems and other forms of adjudication have returned to functionality in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic. In general, courts have continued to work through the case backlog caused by the Covid-19 pandemic and, during the year ended December 31, 2025, we have observed continuing portfolio activity. Nevertheless, some court systems continue to face backlogs, delaying adjudication. Inevitably, some of our matters (and thus our cash realizations from them) in jurisdictions impacted by court backlogs have been slowed by these dynamics, and we saw impact from that in our 2025 financial results as extensions of expected duration reduced the fair value of certain assets. In some cases, we are protected on duration risk, because some of our assets have time-based terms that increase our absolute returns as time passes. We have not seen the discontinuance of any matters. Of our concluded matters since June 2021, we have observed a higher incidence of pre-adjudication settlements as a proportion of aggregate realizations in comparison to the period from our inception to June 2021. We do not yet know whether this is an effect of the Covid-19 pandemic or a lasting trend.

The effect of inflation on our revenues is mitigated to a significant extent by a number of factors, including the high returns generated by capital provision assets and their relatively short weighted average lives. Furthermore, inflationary increases in legal case fees and expenses can increase the size of commitments, deployments and damages sought. Because returns on most of our assets are at least partially based upon a multiple of those fees and expenses, our returns on successful cases should also increase in such circumstances. To the degree that inflation drives higher interest rates and to the extent that pre- and post-judgment interest rates in a particular jurisdiction are tied to market interest rates, higher inflation would result in increases in awards by the relevant courts. The effect of inflation on our expenses would predominantly be through employee costs, which represent the majority of our operating expenses, although a significant portion of compensation-related expenses are performance-based. Our Principal Finance costs include interest expenses associated with our outstanding debt securities, although these are fixed coupon and non-adjustable, regardless of the rate of inflation.

Litigation outcomes stand apart from the remainder of the conventional credit universe because they do not arise as a result of a contractual relationship between the judgment debtor and creditor, unlike essentially all other forms of credit obligation. Thus, for example, a debtholder seeking recovery on a defaulted debt must take many steps, typically involving notice, a cure period and usually a subsequent judicial or insolvency proceeding that will generally sweep in other creditors, resulting in a meaningful risk of the debt being impaired or compromised. By contrast, a judgment creditor has immediate and unfettered rights of action, for example, to seize assets and garnish cash flows, meaning that a judgment creditor often has substantial leverage and ability to secure payment of a judgment against even a financially distressed
judgment debtor as long as the judgment debtor does not seek protection from creditors in a formal insolvency proceeding.

To the extent that the claimant in a matter we are financing becomes insolvent, insolvency proceedings typically provide for the continued prosecution of claims given that the claim is a valuable contingent asset, the recovery of which is in the best interests of the claimant's stakeholders, and we are often a secured creditor with respect to the litigation we are financing. Nevertheless, a claimant's insolvency may delay the underlying litigation while the insolvency process unfolds. Judgment creditors are typically unsecured creditors, and should the defendant in a matter we are financing become insolvent, the risk to our recovery is dependent on the financial condition of the judgment debtor and the availability of assets for unsecured creditors.

paragraphs: Burford 是全球規模最大的專注於提供資本的公司，根據投資組合規模，針對訴訟及法律資產的基礎價值，我們俗稱為法律金融。

我們是一家全球性公司，透過提供多樣化的金融產品與服務來服務法律產業。我們最大的業務是為參與持續訴訟的客戶提供資本，他們可以用來支付訴訟費用及相關開支，並實現訴訟預期未來價值的現金化。我們專注於大型、複雜的訴訟，而非通常由消費者或小型企業追訴的小規模訴訟。我們很少參與資本低於 500 萬美元的交易，並經常提供數倍於此金額的資本，高達數十億美元。自 2009 年成立以來，我們在集團層面已承諾逾 121 億美元的法律金融資產。

我們的客戶包括全球許多最大的企業與律師事務所。法律金融讓當事人可以選擇他們喜好的律師事務所，而不需預付費用，並能根據企業的偏好時間表加速部分預期賠償的現金化。此外，法律金融可能讓當事人避免將法律費用列為營運費用，進而改善淨收入指標，同時透過現金化法律資產提高流動性，這些資產否則不會反映在其財務報表中。法律金融讓律師事務所即使在採用風險費或替代費用模式接案時，也能獲得現金來運作業務並支付律師薪資。它也讓偏好按小時計費的律師事務所能競爭風險費或替代費用的業務。根據《美國律師》2025 年收入排名，我們已接獲 100 家最大美國律師事務所中的 95 家的融資詢問或與其展開潛在新業務，並與 100 家最大全球律師事務所中的 93 家以及大型區域律師事務所與訴訟專門律師事務所合作。
我們主要透過資產負債表使用小幅槓桿來資金融資法律金融投資組合，目標是再投資所得以增長並複利回報。我們的主要融資活動由第三方資本透過私人基金補充，我們從此獲得資產管理收入。
目前，我們管理的集團層面法律金融投資組合為 75 億美元。我們的投資組合根據地理區域與法律聲請類型進行分散，我們認為這是全球規模最大的類型。在過去 16 年中，與我們成立時籌集的 1.3 億美元相比，已成長超過 50 倍。
在一個持續成長與演進的產業中，我們認為我們享有顯著的競爭優勢，這歸功於我們長期以來產生強勁回報的紀錄、來自數千個案例的成長自有數據集，用以指導最佳的風險評估決策、我們的資產負債表規模、資金來源的多樣性、團隊的品質以及品牌認知度。
除了法律金融，我們認為在法律產業的業務中，提供某些額外的服務方案也為我們公司帶來成長機會與潛力。

我們由母公司 Burford Capital Limited 及多個在不同司法管轄區設立的全資子公司組成，這些子公司進行我們的業務運作並部署資金。Burford Capital LLC 是 Burford Capital Limited 的全資間接子公司，並為我們在美國的主要營運公司；Burford Capital (UK) Limited 是 Burford Capital Limited 的全資間接子公司，並為我們在英國的主要營運公司。這兩個實體為其他集團公司提供各種企業及投資諮詢服務。我們的母公司 Burford Capital Limited 沒有業務或員工。請參閱「—組織架構」以取得更多關於我們組織架構的資訊。

2009年，我們的創始人發起設立Burford，共同抱持著一個願景，即建立一個由永久資本支撐的機構，能提供客製化融資，協助企業與律師事務所應對當時在管理法律費用時所面臨的重大經濟挑戰。當時，針對此投資提案的資本提供者寥寥無幾，且多為英國境內的機構，因先前司法體系改革已允許第三方資本參與提供多種法律服務。因此，儘管投資顧問團隊設立於美國，Burford Capital Limited仍於2009年9月11日於蓋爾尼勳爵（"Guernsey"）註冊為一家封閉式基金公司（limited by shares），並計畫透過發行新股份於倫敦證券交易所上市。隨後

對我們資本提案的需求增加，使得封閉式基金結構無法充分應對市場機會。2012年，我們股東投票支持將Burford重新組建為一家單一、專業性金融營運公司。此重新組建使我們能募集更多債務資本以支持成長，而這在封閉式基金結構下是無法實現的。2014年至2018年間，我們透過倫敦證券交易所主市場上市的債券發行，共募集了6.93億美元，且我們的資本提供資產公允價值成長超過6倍。因美國法律融資資產的本位幣為美元，而英國債券市場無法提供足夠的美元資金，我們尋求信用評級以進入美國私人債務市場，並於2019年10月獲得穆迪（Moody's）的首個企業家族評級，以及2019年11月標準普爾（Standard & Poor's）的長期債務評級。

我們也透過戰略收購來支持非營運性成長。我們於2011年收購Firstassist Legal Expenses Insurance，這是一家英國知名的訴訟費用保險提供者，為我們在倫敦建立據點，並成為我們傳統的不利費用保險業務基礎。我們於2015年收購一家商業智慧公司Focus Intelligence Ltd，使我們能為客戶提供判決執行服務，以處理其資助的爭議。我們於2016年收購GKC Holdings, LLC，這是一家以法律為重點的資產管理公司，並在美國證券交易委員會（SEC）註冊為投資顧問，成為我們資產管理業務的初始核心，同時也擴展了我們在美國的據點與處理專利爭議融資的能力。

為進一步發展我們在美國資本市場的地位，2020年，Burford Capital Limited向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）註冊為一間"外資私人發行人"，這使我們得以發行年度合併財務報表（Form 20-F）與間歇性簡化合併財務報表（Form 6-K），並免除部分適用於美國本土上市公司的規定。我們於2020年10月19日成功取得紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）的普通股上市資格，代碼為"BUR"。隨後，我們的子公司透過Rule 144A與Regulation S（根據證券法）進行私人發行，發行了14億美元的債務證券。有關我們債務證券的更多資訊，請參閱本2025年Form 10-K財務報表中第12節（債務）的說明。
我們於2024年6月30日判定，本公司普通股的絕大多數持有者位於美國，因此自2025年1月1日起，我們不再符合"外資私人發行人"的資格。我們現在需遵守與大多數美國本土上市公司在紐約證券交易所上市相同的披露與財務報告要求。
我們的註冊地址為蓋爾尼勳爵Oak House，Hirzel Street，St. Peter Port，Guernsey GY1 2NP。我們在註冊地址的電話號碼為+44 1481 723 450。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，係針對2025年12月31日財務年度，與2024年12月31日財務年度比較。此討論應與我們的合併財務報表及相關附註說明一併閱讀，內容載於本2025年Form 10-K之其他部分。
以下討論與分析亦包含對某些未經審計的KPI（如下所定義）及非GAAP財務指標的討論，這些KPI及非GAAP財務指標為管理階層用以監測我們財務狀況及營運成果。這些KPI及非GAAP財務指標為補充性資訊，不得與我們根據美國GAAP所報告的合併財務狀況或營運成果孤立看待、取代或優於。有關KPI及非GAAP財務指標及相關重會資訊，請參閱「—財務資訊呈現基礎」及「—重會」。
2024年12月31日財務年度，我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，可於我們2024年12月31日財務年度的Form 10-K年報「管理階層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」部分找到，該年報於2025年3月3日向證券交易委員會提交。

我們的投資組合報酬率受司法活動影響，我們認為這些報酬率通常與市場狀況或總體經濟表現無關聯。經濟與市場狀況對我們業務的最直接影響，與我們的債務成本及企業債務資本市場的取得難易度有關，以及市場利率的變動會導致對我們資產公允價值所應用的折現率調整，並影響我們根據美國GAAP所確認的季度營收。我們認為我們能維持企業債務資本市場的取得，這由穆迪於2025年第二季的信用評級升級、標準普爾於2025年第三季的信用評級升級，以及2025年7月及2026年1月成功發行債務所證明。總體而言，我們認為我們的業務模式
特別能抵禦經濟與市場週期的影響，這是因為驅動我們營收與現金流的資產性質。
更廣泛而言，經濟狀況可能影響我們所考慮資金融資的訴訟案件數量與類型。例如，企業破產率增加可能導致資金融資與破產或財務困難相關的訴訟機會；較高的利率或其它形式的經濟壓力可能導致企業非法行為（例如共謀固定價格），導致可資融資的聲請；股東與市場的壓力可能導致證券詐欺及其他類似行為，再次導致可資融資的聲請。
在2025年12月31日財務年度，全球貿易中斷的潛在風險因關稅的實施而顯著增加，導致全球金融市場出現大幅波動。我們不認為全球關稅率的廣泛提高會對我們法律金融投資組合或財務結果產生重大影響。雖然目前貿易關稅的經濟影響尚不確定，但較緊縮的金融條件及國內生產總值的減弱通常會導致企業爭議及相關訴訟案件的增加，儘管這種情況通常會有延遲。
請參閱「風險因素—與我們業務及產業相關的風險—我們的各種法律金融資產可能產生信用風險，可能對我們業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或流動性產生不利影響」及「風險因素—與我們業務及產業相關的風險—法律、政治及經濟不確定性可能對公共衛生威脅的影響、嚴重程度及持續時間產生不利影響，可能對我們業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或流動性產生不利影響」。

法院系統及其他形式的裁決已於 Covid-19 疫情後恢復正常運作。總體而言，法院持續處理因 Covid-19 疫情所造成的案件積壓，於 2025 年度結訖的會計期間，我們觀察到持續的投資組合活動。然而，部分法院系統仍面臨案件積壓，延宕裁決。不可避免地，部分我們的案件（以及因此來自這些案件的現金回報）在受法院積壓影響的司法管轄區已因這些情況而延遲，我們在 2025 年財務結果中觀察到此影響，因預期執行時間延長而降低某些資產的公允價值。在某些情況下，我們對執行時間風險有所保障，因為部分資產具有時間基礎的條款，隨著時間推移，我們的絕對回報會增加。我們尚未觀察到任何案件中止。自 2021 年 6 月以來，我們觀察到預裁決和解的比例較我們成立至 2021 年 6 月期間的總回報比例更高。我們尚未確定這是否為 Covid-19 疫情的影響或長期趨勢。
請參閱 "風險因素—與我們業務及產業相關的風險—公共衛生威脅的影響、嚴重程度及持續時間所帶來的法律、政治與經濟不確定性可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及/或流動性產生負面影響"。

通貨膨脹對我們收入的影響，因多種因素而大幅緩解，包括高報酬率的資本提供資產及其相對較短的加權平均使用壽命。此外，法律案件費用及支出的通貨膨脹性增加，可能提高承諾、部署及損害賠償的規模。因為大多數我們資產的報酬至少部分基於這些費用及支出的倍數，因此在這種情況下，我們成功案件的報酬應也會增加。若通貨膨脹導致利率上升，且特定司法管轄區的預判決及判決後利息率與市場利率掛鉤，則通貨膨脹將導致相關法院的賠償金額增加。通貨膨脹對我們費用的影響，主要透過員工成本，而員工成本為我們營運費用的絕大部分，雖然一筆相當大的補償相關費用為績效掛鉤。我們的本金融資成本包括與我們現有債務證券相關的利息費用，雖然這些為固定票面利率且不隨通貨膨脹率調整。

訴訟結果與傳統信用宇宙的其他部分有所不同，因為它們並非基於判決債務人與債權人之間的契約關係，與幾乎所有其他形式的信用義務不同。因此，例如，一個債權人若要追討 defaulted 債務，必須進行許多步驟，通常包括通知、補救期及通常後續的司法或破產程序，該程序通常會納入其他債權人，導致債務有相當風險被減損或妥協。相較之下，判決債權人擁有立即且不受限制的行動權利，例如，可以扣押資產及剝奪現金流，意味著判決債權人通常擁有相當大的優勢及能力，可確保判決的執行，即使判決債務人財務困難，只要判決債務人未尋求正式破產程序的債權人保護。
若我們所資助的案件中，請求人成為破產，則破產程序通常會繼續進行該請求，因為該請求為一價值可實現的或有資產，其回收對請求人的股東最有利，而我們通常為該訴訟的有擔保債權人。然而，請求人的破產可能延宕訴訟的進行，直到破產程序完成。判決債權人通常為無擔保債權人，若我們所資助的案件中被告成為破產，則我們的回收風險取決於判決債務人的財務狀況及無擔保債權人可取得的資產。
若我們所資助的案件中，請求人成為破產，則破產程序通常會繼續進行該請求，因為該請求為一價值可實現的或有資產，其回收對請求人的股東最有利，而我們通常為該訴訟的有擔保債權人。然而，請求人的破命可能延宕訴訟的進行，直到破產程序完成。判決債權人通常為無擔保債權人，若我們所資助的案件中被告成為破產，則我們的回收風險取決於判決債務人的財務狀況及無擔保債權人可取得的資產。

paragraphs: 投資本公司的證券涉及風險。投資本公司的證券者應謹慎考量下列風險，以及本 2025 年 10-K 表及我們其他報告中所包含的其他資訊，這些報告是我們不時向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交或提供給 SEC 的。任何下列風險都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或流動性產生重大且不利的影響。我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或流動性也可能因適用於所有公司的其他因素，以及我們目前未知或認為不重要的其他風險而受到重大且不利的影響。在任何情況下，我們的證券交易價格都可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資於本公司證券的金額。雖然我們可能根據認為可行且合理的程度，努力緩解已知風險，但我們無法提供任何保證，也未作出任何陳述，表示我們的緩解措施（如有）會成功。請參閱「前瞻性陳述」、「業務」及「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之分析」，以取得有關可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或流動性產生重大且不利影響的某些業務、競爭、監管、市場、經濟及其他條件的額外資訊。
▪訴訟結果具有風險且難以預測，且在訴訟事項中遭受損失，可能會導致與該事項相關的全部資本損失。
▪我們的收入、獲利及現金流可能在不同期間有重大變動，因為訴訟事項的解決時間及結果均難以預測。
▪我們的成功取決於我們識別並選擇合適的法律融資資產以進行融資的能力，若我們未能做到，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或流動性產生重大且不利的影響。
▪若我們無法防止因網路安全事件、未經授權使用或竊取而導致機密資訊、智慧財產權、訴訟或業務策略的不當使用或揭露，或未經授權存取，則我們的業務及營運可能會受到影響。
▪我們用來預測法律融資資產回報及營運的機率模型及決策科學工具，包括人工智慧技術，若其不準確或失敗，可能會對我們的業務產生重大且不利的影響。
